mechanism: "dns" is a DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS row (src/config-options.lisp:442) and grep finds no other occurrence in src/: there is no fNameLookup equivalent. BL.NET:MAKE-TCP-CONNECTION (src/networking/connection.lisp:238-281) asks PROXY-FOR-TARGET first; with no proxy it passes the raw HOST string to USOCKET:SOCKET-CONNECT, which on SBCL resolves it through SB-BSD-SOCKETS:GET-HOST-BY-NAME, i.e. the host resolver. Core at d3056bc gates exactly this: fNameLookup = GetBoolArg("-dns", DEFAULT_NAME_LOOKUP) (src/init.cpp:1696, default true in src/netbase.h:28), and CConnman::ConnectNode resolves a named destination with Lookup(pszDest, default_port, fNameLookup && !HaveNameProxy(), 256) (src/net.cpp:406). With -dns=0 and no name proxy that Lookup returns empty, the invalid addrConnect is pushed into connect_to, the per-target loop finds neither a valid address nor a name proxy, and the target is never dialed. Core applies fNameLookup to four more resolutions we also do eagerly: -torcontrol (torcontrol.cpp:156), -proxy (init.cpp:1722), -onion (init.cpp:1778), -externalip (init.cpp:1804) and -i2psam (init.cpp:2234). The proxy half of Core's condition IS honoured here: with a proxy configured the name goes into the SOCKS5 CONNECT as ATYP DOMAINNAME and never to the local resolver (src/networking/socks5.lisp, and the docstring at connection.lisp:246-252 states it), and %REACHABLE-SEED-ADDRESSES (src/node/peers.lisp:160-199) deliberately keeps seed HOSTNAMES unresolved under a proxy for the same reason. Named dial targets reach this path: %SPLIT-ADDED-NODE-SPEC (src/node/peers.lisp:851) accepts a bare "host", and CONNECT-PEER (src/networking/peer.lisp:330) hands it straight to MAKE-TCP-CONNECTION.
consequence: An operator who sets -dns=0 -- the documented way to stop the node making plaintext DNS queries -- still emits one resolver query per named -addnode / -connect / -seednode target, disclosing to whatever resolver the host uses (and to anyone on that path) which peers this node is configured to reach. Bounded on three sides: the option is explicitly supplied, so the startup WARN names it (measured: SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS returns "dns"); with -proxy configured -- the configuration in which a DNS leak actually matters -- the name already goes through the tunnel and no local lookup happens; and an operator who dials IP literals only, which is what -dns=0 users normally do, is unaffected because no resolution is attempted for a literal. Kept at S3 rather than raised: no funds are at risk, the privacy loss is confined to configuration the operator typed and to the no-proxy case, and it is announced at startup.
evidence: Executed in the project container (worktree /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-options-s3, warm image, probe ga11probe/p-rest.lisp, function P-DNS). (a) With BL.NET:*PROXY* bound to NIL, (bl.net:make-tcp-connection "ga11-no-such-host-xyz.invalid" 8333 :timeout 2) SIGNALLED USOCKET:NS-HOST-NOT-FOUND-ERROR -- the name-service error raised by the host resolver -- proving the local resolver was consulted from inside our function; a bare (usocket:socket-connect "ga11-no-such-host-xyz.invalid" 8333 ...) in the same image raises the identical condition, identifying the resolution site. (b) With BL.NET:*PROXY* bound to a proxy on 127.0.0.1:1 the same call RETURNED (NIL T) -- no connection, proxy-connection-failed T -- with no name-service condition at all, so the name was never resolved locally. (c) (bl.cfg::core-only-option-p "dns") => T, and START-NODE-PLIST with -dns=0 among its arguments returned (:LISTEN T :WALLET-NAMES NIL :NETWORK :REGTEST) with "dns" in SUPPLIED-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS. Incidental observation from (a), outside this finding: MAKE-TCP-CONNECTION's handler-case catches only USOCKET:SOCKET-ERROR and USOCKET:TIMEOUT-ERROR, so a resolution failure escapes to the caller as a condition instead of returning NIL. Sources: src/config-options.lisp:442; src/networking/connection.lisp:238-281; src/networking/peer.lisp:330, 1194; src/node/peers.lisp:160-199, 851; refs/bitcoin/src/init.cpp:1696, 1722, 1778, 1804, 2234; refs/bitcoin/src/net.cpp:399-432; refs/bitcoin/src/netbase.h:23,28; refs/bitcoin/src/netbase.cpp:37; refs/bitcoin/src/torcontrol.cpp:156.
fix_shape: Promote "dns" out of DEFINE-CORE-ONLY-OPTIONS into a real DEFINE-OPTION boolean defaulting to true, bind it to a networking special (bl.net:*name-lookup*, Core's fNameLookup) in the startup path, and put Core's whole condition -- fNameLookup && !HaveNameProxy() -- in one place: a RESOLVE-DIAL-TARGET helper in src/networking/connection.lisp that MAKE-TCP-CONNECTION calls before USOCKET:SOCKET-CONNECT. When a proxy applies, keep today's behaviour exactly (hand the name to SOCKS5, resolve nothing). When no proxy applies and the target is not an address literal, resolve only if *name-lookup* is true; otherwise refuse the dial the way PROXY-FOR-TARGET's refusal branch already does at connection.lisp:268-270, with a log-debug line, so the caller sees NIL rather than a condition. Apply the same flag to the other resolutions Core gates with it -- -torcontrol, -proxy, -onion, -externalip, -i2psam -- since gating only the dial path would leave the leak the option exists to close. A test should assert that with *name-lookup* NIL and no proxy a hostname target returns NIL without signalling a name-service condition, with the *name-lookup* T case as the positive control.
